item.title: Democrats Nominate Jeffries as Speaker, Making History
item.description: The vote put Representative Hakeem Jeffries of New York in line to become the first Black lawmaker to win the post second in line to the presidency.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:description: Representative Hakeem Jeffries met with almost all members and newly elected Democrats in recent days as he sought to wrap up his nomination with as little opposition as possible.

item.title: A Massachusetts Town Revolts Against Amazon’s Delivery Drones
item.description: Amazon wants to offer fast delivery. Residents want quiet skies. A Massachusetts suburb wages an epic battle over control of its airspace.
item.dc:creator: Juliet Macur and Sophie Park
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times

item.title: How Mary Peltola Triumphed in Alaska’s Senate Race
item.description: Beleaguered by high fuel costs and wary of overfishing, Alaskans were drawn to the Democrat’s hyperlocal pitch.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning and Emily Schwing
item.media:description: Mary Peltola at her watch party in Anchorage earlier this month.

item.title: House Democrats Cast Wide Net as They Prepare Trump Investigations
item.description: The inquiries would focus on President Trump, his family and top officials in his administration and would include a look at Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and policies related to Nvidia.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:description: Representative Robert Garcia, Democrat of California, sent a dozen notices to members of President Trump’s family and current and former administration officials asking them to preserve documents on investigative targets.

item.title: Putin Will Continue Ukraine War Despite Plans to Meet Trump, Intelligence Says
item.description: President Trump plans to discuss Ukraine with the leaders of Russia and China. He has halted some sanctions on Russia and announced that the United States will buy Russian diesel.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong, Julian E. Barnes and Jeanna Smialek
item.media:credit: Finbarr O'Reilly for The New York Times
item.media:description: Ukrainian forces near frontline positions in Ukraine’s eastern Kharkiv region last month.

item.title: American A.I. Models Have Potential to Be Turned Against U.S., Study Finds
item.description: An investigation by the Government Accountability Office found that researchers were able to prod chatbots into generating data that could be used in planning or conducting mass-casualty attacks.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz
item.category: Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
item.media:description: The study, conducted in the spring at the request of Senator Maggie Hassan, Democrat of New Hampshire, involved chatbots from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI.

item.title: Fans Flock to the Hollywood Sign. Neighbors Say, Get Off My Road.
item.description: The residents of the Hollywood Hills have sued Los Angeles, saying the city has not done enough to address the dangerous conditions created by tourists vying for a glimpse of the iconic Hollywood sign.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín
item.media:credit: Mark Abramson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sightseers catching a view of the Hollywood sign. A crush of tourists has created traffic that jams the narrow roads in the surrounding hills.

item.title: U.S. Catholic Bishops Are Discussing A.I. at Annual Meeting
item.description: At their annual fall meeting, the bishops are discussing how to address the negative impacts of A.I., even as some struggle to navigate the fast-evolving technology.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Dias
item.media:description: Pope Leo established a new Vatican commission on A.I. this year.

item.title: Trump Administration Presses Ahead in Legal Battle Over U.S. Attorneys
item.description: A judge has ruled that Bill Essayli was acting “unlawfully” as U.S. attorney in Los Angeles. He is one of three prosecutors appointed by the Trump administration through a unique process.
item.dc:creator: Danny Hakim
item.media:description: Bill Essayli was among a group of President Trump’s allies who were initially appointed “interim” U.S. attorneys last year.

item.title: Democrats Claim 56 Senate Seats After Mary Peltola Wins in Alaska
item.description: Mary Peltola defeated Senator Dan S. Sullivan, a two-term incumbent, to become the first Democrat to represent the conservative state in the Senate since 2015.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning
item.media:credit: Ash Adams for The New York Times
item.media:description: Ms. Peltola will become the first Democrat to represent Alaska in the Senate since 2015.

item.title: A.I. Mistook a Bag of Chips for a Gun, Teenagers’ Lawsuit Says
item.description: Four students of a high school in Baltimore are suing after the police handcuffed and searched them because an artificial intelligence gun-detection system wrongly alerted a bag of Doritos.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Sinco Kelleher
item.media:description: Kenwood High School in Baltimore. Last year, four students there were waiting for a ride home after football practice when the police arrived with guns drawn.

item.title: White House Withdraws Nomination of Heidi Overton to Be F.D.A. Commissioner
item.description: The Senate health committee was scheduled to vote on her nomination Wednesday morning after wrestling with concerns about her stance on abortion and vaccines.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett
item.media:description: Dr. Heidi Overton during a Senate committee hearing in September.

item.title: After Days of Digital Outages, Americans Wonder if the Country Is Breaking
item.description: The digital outages that began on Thursday may not be linked, but they have left Americans with a sense that the nation is off-kilter, with no one ready to fix it.
item.dc:creator: Sabrina Tavernise, Georgia Gee and Madaleine Rubin
item.media:description: Flights were halted for hours on Friday after officials issued a nationwide ground stop.

item.title: F.A.A. Shelves Routers Like the One Linked to the Nationwide Ground Stop
item.description: Federal officials said they believed that a router made by Juniper Networks caused a data overload that disrupted communications.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.category: Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
item.media:credit: Justin L. Stewart for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Los Angeles airport on Friday. A nationwide ground stop caused havoc for travelers and airlines.

item.title: Markwayne Mullin Defends Flight to L.S.U.-Texas Game After Ground Stop
item.description: “We still gotta live our lives,” said the homeland security secretary, who is required to use government planes for personal travel. His department said he paid.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, spoke to reporters outside the White House on Friday.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries Embraces Medicare Expansion on Eve of Speaker Vote
item.description: The top House Democrat endorsed lowering the eligibility age, covering all children and adding vision, hearing and dental services, proposals seen as precursors to Medicare for All.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.category: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (2010)
item.media:description: Representative Hakeem Jeffries, Democrat of New York, is expected to be nominated for speaker. Before the election, he did not endorse a plan to phase in Medicare for All. But with the Democrats’ sweeping gains, he appears to be taking a more ambitious approach.

item.title: For Democrats, a Leadership Fight Is Marring an Electoral Triumph
item.description: The contest between Senators Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen to be majority leader is sowing party divisions and putting them on public display.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold and Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the minority leader, at a news conference at the Capitol on Tuesday.

item.title: Democrats Assail RFK Jr. After U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status
item.description: Incoming senators and prospective presidential candidates blamed the health secretary’s history of vaccine skepticism for the rise of measles in the country.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:description: In a statement on Tuesday, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the health secretary, vowed to “stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain U.S. measles elimination status.”

item.title: Trump Administration Says It Will Not Use Ships to Deport Migrants
item.description: The Homeland Security Department told Congress of the decision after The New York Times reported last month that it was considering deportations by sea.
item.dc:creator: Aishvarya Kavi
item.media:description: Training Ship Golden Bear was used for more than three decades as a classroom at sea, carrying cadets studying at a maritime academy across the Pacific Ocean.

item.title: Iran Is Emboldened After Trump and GOP’s Election Losses, Officials Say
item.description: Iran’s negotiating position has hardened since the midterms, U.S. and other Western officials say. An American lawmaker warned that Iran felt “strategically empowered.”
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Dustin Volz and Farnaz Fassihi
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: A banner depicting Steve Witkoff, President Trump, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Vice President JD Vance was set on fire during a demonstration in Tehran this month.

item.title: Waymo Pulls Its Driverless Taxis From All U.S. Freeways Temporarily
item.description: The move came after California’s Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the cars off the state’s freeways, citing an “imminent hazard to public safety.”
item.dc:creator: Nicole Stock and Tim Arango
item.media:description: A Waymo car on a freeway in California last month. The cars were barred from the state’s freeways last week.

item.title: With House Democratic Majority Still Growing, Recounts Are Starting in Closest Races
item.description: The exact size of the Democratic majority in Congress was undetermined as recounts were sought in two races in North Carolina and one in Minnesota two weeks after the elections.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:description: Democrats secured a 257th seat after a race call in North Carolina on Tuesday, but some races remain uncalled.

item.title: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
item.description: The discovery by security company Calif shows A.I.’s ability to find gaping security holes in popular software. The Java flaw pointed to vulnerabilities in systems used by nearly all Fortune 500 companies.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz and Dylan Freedman
item.media:credit: Saumya Khandelwal for The New York Times
item.media:description: Calif, a tech start-up, said it had used OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Cyber model to uncover a critical software bug in Java.

item.title: Ukraine Talks Run Up Against Deep Enmity Between Russia and Europe
item.description: President Trump’s envoys are trying to overcome Russian hostility and European suspicion to craft a postwar security agreement in Europe that could end the war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski
item.media:description: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on their way to a meeting with a Russian delegation in Moscow last week.

item.title: A Death Along Lake Superior Revives Memories of ‘the Gales of November’
item.description: A 62-year-old man was found drowned in a cove this month, evoking the lake’s stormy history.
item.dc:creator: Christine Hauser

item.title: Hegseth Nominates His Former Aide to Lead the Army
item.description: After months of delay, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the White House have sent Gen. Christopher LaNeve’s nomination for Army chief of staff to the Senate.

item.title: Man Indicted in Bomb Threat at Illinois Ethanol Plant
item.description: A federal grand jury in Peoria charged the man, who may have worked at the BioUrja plant, with threatening to detonate an explosive device last week.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith
item.media:credit: Matt Dayhoff/USA Today Network, via Reuters
item.media:description: The BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant in Peoria, Ill.

item.title: I.R.S. Opens Criminal Probes as Part of Trump’s Pursuit of Left-Wing Groups
item.description: An internal I.R.S. memo viewed by The New York Times reveals how the agency is carrying out President Trump’s orders to investigate “domestic terrorism.”
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
item.media:description: Under an order by President Trump after the killing of Charlie Kirk, the I.R.S. was told to investigate whether nonprofits were “directly or indirectly financing political violence or domestic terrorism.”

item.title: Republicans Recoil as Duffy Outlines $50 Billion Request for Air Traffic Improvements
item.description: The one-page explanation, which he discussed with Republican senators, was thin on details and included many items outside air traffic control.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:description: Mr. Duffy first voiced the demand for $50 billion Friday night during a news conference about a nationwide ground stop that led to air travel disruptions across the East Coast.

item.title: Classified N.S.A. Network Goes Down, Causing Work Disruptions
item.description: There are currently no signs that the outage is the result of a cyberattack or other nefarious activity, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz
item.media:description: The National Security Agency headquarters in Fort Meade, Md.

item.title: Schools Are Closing Nationwide as Enrollment Drops. Parents Are Livid.
item.description: With fewer babies being born and more school choice, districts across the country have concluded they must downsize. Families are trying to push back.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mervosh and Jack Healy
item.media:credit: Jordan Gale for The New York Times
item.media:description: Students protested a school closure plan in Portland, Ore.

item.title: Measles Is Officially Back in the United States. What Now?
item.description: It may take years for the country to regain elimination status. In the meantime, communities will need to adopt numerous strategies to protect people.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli and Dani Blum
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:credit: Desiree Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: A patient with a measles rash in Texas last year. The number of cases in the United States this year has topped 5,400, more than double last year’s tally and the highest since 1991, nearly a decade before the country attained elimination status.

item.title: His Body Was Crushed in a Car Accident. His Artistry Brought Him Back.
item.description: Paul Madonna, known for his drawings of San Francisco landmarks, has recovered enough to have his own art exhibition four years after nearly dying in a head-on collision.
item.dc:creator: Heather Knight
item.media:credit: Austin Leong for The New York Times
item.media:description: Paul Madonna in his studio.
